# The best way to solve this Wordle

**Short answer:** On this word list, the method that mattered was **always guessing a word that fits every clue so far**. With that rule, every opener I tried solved all of its games in 3–5 guesses. Twenty games per opener could not show that any opener was better than another.

## What was tested

The tool's list has 3,000 made-up words, not English ones. Every word contains 2 or 3 of a, e, i, o, u, y. The most common letters are **u, a, o, i, y, k, z, v**, and English favourites like e, s and t are rare. That gave three openers to compare:

- **`akuzo`**: the opener whose letters cover the most words in this list.
- **`akuzo` then `nivyl`**: two fixed openers covering 10 different common letters.
- **`terva`**: an English-style opener, like CRATE.

Each opener played the same 20 games (seeds 1–20), 60 games in total. After the opener, the agent guessed a word that fit every clue so far. Agents chose every guess themselves; grep was used only to list the words that still fit the clues.

## Results

| Strategy | Mean guesses | Failures | Games in 3 / 4 / 5 guesses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `akuzo` | 3.65 | 0/20 | 9 / 9 / 2 |
| `akuzo` + `nivyl` | 3.65 | 0/20 | 8 / 11 / 1 |
| `terva` | 3.75 | 0/20 | 9 / 7 / 4 |

The table below compares openers game by game on the same seeds. A negative difference means the first strategy needed fewer guesses. The ranges are 95% bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples, random seed 20261027).

| Comparison | Mean difference (95% range) |
|---|---|
| `akuzo` − `terva` | −0.10 [−0.55, 0.35] |
| `akuzo`+`nivyl` − `akuzo` | 0.00 [−0.30, 0.30] |
| `akuzo`+`nivyl` − `terva` | −0.10 [−0.40, 0.20] |

Every range includes zero. The merge step also produced a chart, `strategy_comparison.png`, which is saved with the study's files.

All of this is recorded in the Science log, under Conclusion `e_0efad464f535` for question `e_20da865e4b44`. A separate review step recalculated every number by hand and found that they all match.

## What this means

- **Fitting every clue is what kept all 60 games under 6 guesses.** I did not test a strategy without this rule, so this is an observation, not a measured comparison.
- **The opener made no measurable difference.** The list-tuned `akuzo` came out 0.1 guesses better than `terva`, but that gap is far smaller than the noise.
